radiology_report:
Radboudumc
Department of Radiology
Date: 12 Feb 2025
Exam: Multiparametric MRI prostate
Clinical indication: PSA 4.8 ng/mL, rising trend, prior biopsy Gleason 4+4. Request for staging and lesion characterization.

FINDINGS:
The prostate volume measures 25.31 mL. The peripheral zone of the right posterolateral aspect contains a 12 mm focal lesion. On T2-weighted imaging, the lesion appears markedly hypointense. Diffusion-weighted imaging demonstrates restricted diffusion with high signal on b=1400 and corresponding low signal on the ADC map. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences show early and intense enhancement of the lesion, preceding the surrounding glandular tissue. No extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion is identified. No suspicious pelvic lymphadenopathy is seen.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right posterolateral peripheral zone, 12 mm in diameter.
PSA density: 0.19 ng/mL/mL.
Clinical T stage: cT2.
csPCa predicted probability 0.8035576.

previous_notes.text:
29 Oct 2024 - Dr. R. Visser (GP):
The patient returned for routine follow-up of his known prostate cancer diagnosis. He reports no new urinary symptoms and continues his weekend hiking routine. Recent blood work shows a PSA of 3.7 ng/mL, which is stable compared to previous measurements. I have arranged for an outpatient urology re-evaluation in early 2025 to discuss the ongoing management plan and review the latest imaging results.

previous_notes.text:
05 Sep 2023 - Dr. R. Visser (GP):
The patient presented with a PSA of 2.9 ng/mL, which has risen slightly from his baseline. He was referred for a prostate biopsy to investigate the cause of the elevation. The biopsy confirmed the presence of prostate cancer, and he has been scheduled for regular monitoring and urology follow-up. I advised him to continue his current lifestyle and to report any new symptoms promptly.

pathology_report:
Biopsy timepoint 1 (Jan 2024):
Histological examination of the prostate biopsy cores reveals adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 4+4, corresponding to ISUP grade group 4. The dominant growth pattern is cribriform. High-risk features are present, specifically cribriform pattern and intraductal carcinoma (IDC-P). The tumour is located in the right side of the prostate.

Summary of trajectory:
The histological findings remain consistent across the available timepoint, showing high-grade disease with ISUP grade group 4 and high-risk morphological features.

AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): grade group 4.
